skill.name: stack-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze project stack and recommend skills. Auto-detects frameworks, activates generic ai-dev-kit skills, and optionally scaffolds project-specific skills in the target repo.
skill.summary: Match a detected technology stack to development skills and optionally scaffold project-specific templates.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: All 61 static alerts are false positives involving Markdown, benign date substitution, a schema identifier, and expected optional repository writes. Scaffolding has a separate overwrite risk because header generation replaces SKILL.md in the current directory rather than the copied destination. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection, credential theft, or data exfiltration in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Scaffolding writes SKILL.md and a predictable temporary file in the current directory instead of the copied destination.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the destination explicitly, quote paths, create temporary files securely there, and require confirmation before replacing existing skill files.

semantic_findings.title: Scaffolding Can Overwrite the Current Skill
semantic_findings.description: The copy command targets the repository, but 'mv temp SKILL.md' and sed modify the current directory without changing to that destination. Running from the skill directory can replace the analyzer instructions with a template and leave the copied skill uncustomized.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example uses relative output paths and never changes directories after copying. The overwrite is clear if followed literally; agent interpretation may differ.

content.user_title: Match Your Project Stack to Development Skills
content.value_statement: Choosing development skills is difficult when a repository uses several technologies. Stack Analyzer maps detected technologies to relevant skills and optional project templates.
actual_capabilities: Uses the library-detection skill to obtain languages, frameworks, databases, test frameworks, and build tools.
Matches dependency names and file patterns against configured skill recommendation rules.
Produces recommendation reports with detected technologies, matching reasons, and skill status.
Supports optional activation of generic ai-dev-kit skills through the surrounding plugin workflow.
Provides research, domain vocabulary, and testing templates for optional project-specific scaffolding.
Documents generated artifacts in a manifest and explains which files persist after plugin removal.
limitations: Requires the separate library-detection skill and surrounding ai-dev-kit integration for the documented workflow.
Recommendations depend on configured rules and detection results, not comprehensive architectural analysis.
Templates contain placeholders; illustrated supporting files and the configured API template are not included in this package.
The scaffolding example has a current-directory overwrite risk and requires correction before use.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository with Stack Analyzer. Report detected technologies and recommended skills without activating skills or changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Each Recommendation
prompt_templates.prompt: Match the detected stack to recommendation rules. Explain the dependency or file evidence for each match and identify unavailable dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Project Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify matching research, domain, and testing templates. List proposed output paths and placeholders for review. Do not copy or overwrite files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Controlled Scaffolding
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a scaffolding plan for approved templates. Use explicit destination paths and protect existing files. Include manifest updates. Wait for approval before writing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review filesystem changes before execution

output_examples.input: Plan project-specific guidance for a repository with domain models and custom test fixtures.
output: Candidate: project-domain for vocabulary, entity relationships, and validation rules, subject to configured detection thresholds.
Candidate: project-testing for fixture usage, test naming, and coverage requirements, subject to configured detection thresholds.
Templates require project-specific customization. Review destination paths and correct the scaffolding overwrite issue before generating files.

best_practices: Start with a report-only review and verify the evidence supporting each recommendation.
Confirm required companion skills and template files are available before activation or scaffolding.
Correct scaffolding paths, preserve existing files, and review the manifest and generated content before committing changes.
anti_patterns: Activating skills for technologies that detection did not identify.
Running the scaffolding example unchanged or overwriting existing project instructions without review.
Treating template placeholders as finished project knowledge or expecting plugin removal to delete generated project files.

faq.question: Does this package detect the stack independently?
faq.answer: No. The workflow first invokes the separate library-detection skill, then matches its results against recommendation rules.

faq.question: Does analysis automatically modify my repository?
faq.answer: Activation and scaffolding default to disabled. The documented report-only workflow does not create project skills.

faq.question: Which project templates are included?
faq.answer: Research, domain vocabulary, and testing templates are included. Their project-specific sections require customization.

faq.question: Can I run the scaffolding commands as written?
faq.answer: Correct the destination handling first. The example can overwrite SKILL.md in the current directory instead of customizing the copied skill.

faq.question: What remains after removing ai-dev-kit?
faq.answer: Project-specific skills and generated documentation can remain. Use the generated manifest to review artifacts before deleting them.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The package declares support for all three. Its documented commands and activation workflow depend on ai-dev-kit integration in your environment.
